newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-GOGELE LEADS SAFRICAN PGA WITH BRILLIANT 64.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GOGELE LEADS SAFRICAN PGA WITH BRILLIANT 64.

text.p: Thomas Gogele of Germany led the South African PGA golf tournament after shooting a brilliant eight under par 64 in the first round on Thursday.

Gogele, 26, led by a shot from Italian Massimo Scarpa and big hitting South African Retief Goosen. A group of players were bunched at six under and Zimbabwe's Nick Price, who won last week in Sun City, was in contention again after a 67.
Gogele took advantage of a few minor swing adjustments made on the range at the beginning of the week and peppered the flag with his iron shots all day.

He started on the 10th hole and went out in four under par 32, then birdied the first two holes of his back nine. His only dropped shot was as the result of hitting his drive behind a tree at the fourth hole, his 13th and he stormed home with birdies on each of the last three holes.
Scarpa, who generally plays right handed, but chips left handed, chipped in at the 13th for one of eight birdies on his card.

Goosen took advantage of the balmy conditions to unleash his characteristic huge drives. He was able to hit wedges into the green at most of the par fours and his sometimes shaky putting stroke stood up to the test.
But it was another frustrating day for Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros who carded a two over par 74 and looked likely to miss his second cut in two weeks.
